An indecomposable permutation is one that cannot be divided into two parts such that the first part is a permutation of \(\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}\) for any \(m < n\). This condition is exactly satisfied if, for every \(k\) from 1 to \(n-1\), the maximum of the first \(k\) elements exceeds \(k\).

The number of indecomposable permutations of \(n\) elements is given by the recurrence relation:
\[
f(n) = n! - \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} f(k) \cdot (n - k)!
\]

Using this recurrence relation, we compute the values step-by-step:
